source.title: When Small Variations Become Big Failures: Reliability Challenges in Compute-in-Memory Neural Accelerators

confidence_rationale: Closest paper to REE's actual concern (deterministic safety boundary in an analog substrate). Concludes minor device variation amplifies through analog MAC into catastrophic accuracy collapse in safety-critical inference, and that hard correctness guarantees cannot presently be assumed -- only enhanced statistical mitigation (SWIM selective verification, right-censored-Gaussian-noise training). arXiv preprint (not yet peer-reviewed), so source_quality discounted.
failure_signatures: Error accumulation across analog MAC operations turns sub-threshold device variation into catastrophic, workload-level failure in safety-critical inference.
Write-verify is described as insufficient for DETERMINISTIC safety guarantees -- the substrate supports soft statistical reliability, not the hard externally-auditable boundary the claim requires.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In compute-in-memory neural accelerators, small device variations cause disproportionately large accuracy degradation in safety-critical tasks; existing write-verify protocols require enhancement to provide deterministic safety guarantees, and the authors propose selective verification (SWIM) plus noise-robust training rather than a hard guarantee.
mapping.ree_translation: Speaks directly to Q-066's AUDITABILITY / hard-safety-gate axis: current analog/in-memory hardware cannot furnish deterministic safety guarantees, so an externally-inspectable hard gate is an open problem, not a solved capability, in this substrate class.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Safety-critical inference accuracy collapse in a CIM DNN accelerator is structurally analogous to but NOT REE's simulated-vs-released action gate; the paper shows the CLASS of guarantee REE needs is currently unmet, not that REE's specific gate fails (no REE substrate exists to test).
mapping.source_context: Reliability/co-design analysis of compute-in-memory neural accelerators for safety-critical inference.

confidence_components.notes: arXiv preprint, March 2026; highest mapping_fidelity of the Q-066 set because its framing (analog substrate vs hard safety guarantee) maps unusually well, but still no REE substrate.
